newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs hold steady, unsurprised by Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs hold steady, unsurprised by Tietmeyer.

text.p: Belgian OLOs held steady at firmer levels on Thursday, quietly reassured though unsurprised by comments from Bundesbank president Tietmeyer who said he did not expect German rates to move in the foreseeable future.

"We're mainly tracking Germany - though the spread has widened slightly as the (negative) French spread with Bunds has (narrowed)," one dealer said. "I'd be happy with a spread of 20 basis points, but the market likes these prices," he added.
By 1400 GMT the benchmark 10-year OLO was yielding 5.94 percent where it had stayed nearly all day, compared to 5.96 percent on Wednesday, its spread up one basis point at 12 bp.

A weaker-than-expected German Ifo business climate index for March gave the market support early on in the session. Volumes remained low, though, with one dealer predicting investors would keep away until the 10-year yield hit 6.10 percent.
Range-trading is predicted at least until Monday's monthly OLO auction where a January 2000 OLO will be on offer for the first time along with the current 10-year benchmark.

Dealers said so far there had been little interest expressed in the new bond, but added that once the paper was in the market there could be some switching into the new issue from existing short term paper.
"It could also be that a market maker tries to squeeze the market higher by bidding a few ticks above the others," one dealer added.
